label: Car Brands
rubric: Brand prestige & heritage · Performance/engineering reputation · Cultural cachet & desirability · Reliability/value reputation
note: Companies and trademarks rather than individuals, so no likeness concerns apply here. Avoid using brand logos as visual assets without checking trademark guidelines.

entries.name: Ferrari
entries.rationale: The most recognized performance marque on earth, with unmatched racing heritage.

entries.name: Porsche
entries.rationale: Rare combination of motorsport pedigree, daily usability, and strong reliability scores.

entries.name: Rolls-Royce
entries.rationale: The global shorthand for luxury itself, essentially uncontested at the top.

entries.name: Lamborghini
entries.rationale: Pure poster-car desirability and the most theatrical design language in the business.

entries.name: Bugatti
entries.rationale: Extreme engineering flagship status, though tiny production limits cultural reach.

entries.name: Mercedes-Benz
entries.rationale: Invented the automobile and still the benchmark for full-range prestige.

entries.name: BMW
entries.rationale: The definitive driver's-car brand with enormous global recognition.

entries.name: Toyota
entries.rationale: The world's largest automaker with a reliability reputation nobody has matched.

entries.name: Aston Martin
entries.rationale: Enormous cultural cachet and beautiful design, held back by commercial instability.

entries.name: Bentley
entries.rationale: Ultra-luxury craftsmanship with genuine racing history behind it.

entries.name: Lexus
entries.rationale: Consistently tops reliability and satisfaction rankings in the luxury segment.

entries.name: Audi
entries.rationale: Quattro rally heritage and clean design, slightly behind its German rivals on prestige.

entries.name: McLaren
entries.rationale: Formula 1 pedigree and elite engineering, but a small and young road-car business.

entries.name: Honda
entries.rationale: Outstanding engineering reputation and durability across an enormous range.

entries.name: Tesla
entries.rationale: Forced the entire industry electric, though build quality reviews are mixed.

entries.name: Land Rover
entries.rationale: Iconic off-road capability and status, undercut by persistent reliability complaints.

entries.name: Volvo
entries.rationale: The definitive safety brand with strong modern design credentials.

entries.name: Jaguar
entries.rationale: Deep design heritage and elegance, but recent decades have been uneven.

entries.name: Volkswagen
entries.rationale: The people's car with genuine icons in the Beetle and Golf.

entries.name: Subaru
entries.rationale: Rally heritage, all-wheel-drive credibility, and unusually loyal owners.

entries.name: Mazda
entries.rationale: Punches above its price on driving feel and design, smaller global footprint.

entries.name: Ford
entries.rationale: Historic significance via mass production plus the Mustang and F-Series icons.

entries.name: Chevrolet
entries.rationale: The Corvette and Camaro carry serious cultural weight for an otherwise mainstream brand.

entries.name: Jeep
entries.rationale: Owns the off-road identity outright, though reliability ratings lag.

entries.name: Maserati
entries.rationale: Genuine Italian prestige and sound, but quality issues have dented the name.

entries.name: Alfa Romeo
entries.rationale: Beloved design and racing history undercut by a difficult reliability record.

entries.name: Cadillac
entries.rationale: Once the byword for luxury in America; prestige has faded internationally.

entries.name: Hyundai
entries.rationale: Rapid quality and design improvement, though heritage and prestige are thin.

entries.name: Kia
entries.rationale: Strong warranties and much-improved design, still building a premium reputation.

entries.name: Nissan
entries.rationale: The GT-R and Z carry real credibility, but the wider lineup rates as unremarkable.
